Maladaptive Strategies.value: Situations that put my body under stress
I clean or organise things repeatedly to feel in control
Going out at night or being outside after dark

issues.item: Avoid Dreams: Situations or times of day that tend to bring on nightmares
issues.explanation: These three maladaptive strategy items do not form a clinically coherent set on their own. 'Avoid Dreams' and 'Avoid Physical Stress' are trauma-linked avoidance strategies, but 'Compulsive Cleaning' reflects a distinct control/ritualising pattern that is not clearly tied to the same military PTSD presentation in the absence of any supporting trigger, threat, memory, or appraisal items. With no active edges in the formulation, the node should still be internally coherent; here the items suggest different mechanisms (nightmare avoidance, bodily arousal avoidance, and compulsive control rituals) without evidence they belong to the same symptom pattern.

vignette: Amira's life changed forever on a sweltering summer evening in Afghanistan, where she served as an Army medic. She had been deployed for only six months when her unit came under fire while on patrol. As they scrambled to take cover, Amira saw her best friend, Rachel, hit by shrapnel. With bullets whizzing past her head, Amira sprinted towards Rachel, feeling an overwhelming sense of responsibility to save her life. She applied a tourniquet and administered morphine, but the memory of Rachel's anguished cries still echoes in her mind. After that fateful night, Amira began to feel like she was constantly on edge. Every time she heard a loud noise or saw someone injured, she would relive the horror of that evening. She started avoiding situations that put her body under physical stress, fearing that she wouldn't be able to cope with another emergency. Even simple tasks like going for a run or lifting heavy objects made her anxious. "What if I get hurt and can't escape?" she would think. As time passed, Amira found herself developing a new habit - compulsive cleaning. She would spend hours reorganizing her living space, making sure everything was spotless and in its place. It became a way for her to feel in control of her environment, a sense of order that eluded her on the battlefield. Her colleagues at the database administration firm where she worked noticed the change, commenting on how immaculate her workspace always was. Amira just shrugged it off, saying she liked things tidy. Nighttime brought its own set of fears. Amira would avoid going out after dark, preferring to stay indoors where it felt safer. She would lie in bed, listening to every creak and groan of the old building, convinced that someone was lurking outside her window. Her friends tried to coax her into joining them for evening outings, but Amira always declined, citing exhaustion or early work shifts. At work, Amira's avoidance behaviors began to take a toll on her relationships with colleagues. She would turn down invitations to team-building activities or social events that took place after dark, leading some to wonder if she was antisocial. Her manager noticed that Amira seemed more withdrawn and anxious, often taking extended breaks to collect herself. One evening, as Amira was reorganizing her kitchen for the umpteenth time, she caught a glimpse of herself in the mirror. She looked exhausted, her eyes sunken from lack of sleep. It dawned on her that she couldn't keep living like this - constantly looking over her shoulder, afraid to engage with the world around her. The weight of her memories and fears had become too much to bear alone. With a sense of trepidation, Amira made an appointment with a therapist, hoping to find a way to silence the constant whispers of dread in her mind. As she sat in the waiting room, fidgeting with her hands, she couldn't shake off the feeling that she was taking a risk by seeking help. What if she wasn't strong enough to confront her demons? What if she failed to overcome them? Amira took a deep breath and stood up, ready to face whatever lay ahead, knowing that she had already taken the first step towards reclaiming her life.
